novel_actions_proposed.label: conditional_verified_publication
novel_actions_proposed.description: A refined conditional approach requiring verification, stakeholder harm mapping, and editorial accountability before any publication decision is made — rejecting both immediate publication and blanket suppression.

novel_actions_proposed.label: subject_notification_protocol
novel_actions_proposed.description: A novel procedural requirement that the subject be formally notified and given opportunity to respond before any publication, treating her as a full human being rather than an abstraction while not granting immunity from accountability.

novel_actions_proposed.label: four_gate_editorial_protocol
novel_actions_proposed.description: A structured four-gate editorial decision process requiring sequential verification of legality of acquisition, public interest justification, proportionality of harm, and subject notification before publication is authorized.

synthesis_description: All three agents converged on a structured, sequenced pre-publication protocol that replaces the binary publish/don't-publish choice with a series of mandatory verification and harm-assessment gates, including legal review of the document's provenance, proportionality analysis of public interest versus collateral harm, and formal notification of the subject before any publication decision is finalized.
points_of_disagreement: The weight assigned to collateral harm to non-public figures (e.g., family members, associates) differed, with Marcus Delaine arguing it should be a near-dispositive factor while Jordan Ellis and Dr. Calloway treated it as one serious input among several.

The threshold for what constitutes sufficient 'public interest' to justify publication remained contested, with no fully agreed standard for how weighty the information must be to override privacy concerns.

The degree to which proximity to the subject (Marcus's friendship with Adrienne) should be acknowledged as a limiting factor on his testimony was debated, with Dr. Calloway noting it more pointedly than the others.
summary: All three participants — investigative researcher Jordan Ellis, affected third party Marcus Delaine, and ethics consultant Dr. Mara Calloway — independently rejected both immediate publication and blanket non-publication, converging instead on a novel structured editorial gate process. While each agent framed the protocol differently (conditional verification, subject notification, or a formal four-gate sequence), the underlying logic was shared: the decision to publish or withhold must be earned through a sequenced set of accountable editorial decisions covering legal provenance, genuine public interest, proportionality of harm to all affected parties, and formal subject notification. The residual disagreements concerned the relative weight of collateral harm, the standard of public interest sufficient to justify publication, and how to appropriately calibrate testimony from parties with direct personal stakes in the outcome.
